content:
The area of triangle \(OAB\) is half the magnitude of the cross product of vectors \(\overrightarrow{OA}\) and \(\overrightarrow{OB}\).

Given:
\[
\overrightarrow{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}, \quad
\overrightarrow{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}
\]

Compute the cross product \(\overrightarrow{OA} \times \overrightarrow{OB}\):
\[
\overrightarrow{OA} \times \overrightarrow{OB} = 
\begin{pmatrix} 
2 \cdot 1 - 3 \cdot (-2) \\ 
3 \cdot (-3) - 1 \cdot 1 \\ 
1 \cdot (-2) - 2 \cdot (-3)
\end{pmatrix}
= \begin{pmatrix} 2 + 6 \\ -9 - 1 \\ -2 + 6 \end{pmatrix}
= \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ -10 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}
\]

Find its magnitude:
\[
\|\overrightarrow{OA} \times \overrightarrow{OB}\| = \sqrt{8^2 + (-10)^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{64 + 100 + 16} = \sqrt{180} = 6\sqrt{5}
\]

The area of the triangle is half this magnitude:
\[
\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 6\sqrt{5} = 3\sqrt{5}
\]

Answer: \(3\sqrt{5}\)
